question: A cup-to-disc ratio of 0.7 is always pathological and indicates glaucomatous optic atrophy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. A CDR of 0.7 alone is not diagnostic of glaucoma. Bilateral symmetry, the rim tissue integrity (ISNT rule), and correlation with visual fields are all needed before labelling this pathological.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. While a CDR >0.6 raises suspicion for glaucoma, a CDR of 0.7 can be a normal variant, especially if symmetric bilaterally. The key is asymmetry between the two eyes (>0.2 difference) and other disc changes.
